 Order

This appeal under Section 173 (1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellant-claimant for enhancement of compensation awarded by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Gwalior (M.P.) in Claim Case No.28/2012 vide award dated 16/04/2014.

Rambabu Parashar vs Amar Singh on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/163864017/
1 2.

Facts relevant and necessary for disposal of this appeal lie in narrow compass: on 03/09/2011 appellant/claimant was going to Banmmore driving tempo slowly then respondent No.1/driver driving Truck No. UP 93T 3178 rashly and negligently came and dashed the tempo of appellant/claimant as a result of which appellant/claimant received grievous injuries on leg and forehead.
He was admitted in Dr. Saxena Nursing Home, Gwalior.
Thereafter, both the knees have been operated and CT scan has also been conducted of head.
Appellant/claimant was admitted in Dr. Saxena Nursing Home, Gwalior from 03/09/2011 to 04/09/2011.
Thereafter, he was admitted in Arogyadham Hospital from 04/09/2011 to 15/09/2011.
Due to fracture in both legs, he is unable to walk.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant/claimant submits that at the time of accident appellant was aged about 40 years of age and earning Rs. 10,000/- per month.
Due to fracture, he could not drive the vehicle.

It is further submitted that appellant/claimant is the only earning member in his family,
therefore, income of the appellant/claimant @ 5000/- per month assessed by the claims Tribunal only for three months is on lower side and therefore, the same needs to be enhanced.
Appellant/claimant has received permanent disability to the extent of 20% which is evident from Ex.P/77 but the Tribunal has not considered the same.

Therefore, learned Tribunal committed error on fact while awarding compensation to the tune of only Rs. 76,974/- whereas, the appeal is filed for enhancement of Rs. 1,20,000/- in addition to the amount awarded.

4. Learned counsel for respondent No.3-Insurance Company supported the award as regard quantum of compensation, however, the liability is not disputed and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.
5.

Upon hearing, counsel for the parties and perusing the impugned award, this Court is of the view that though Tribunal is not found to have committed any illegality or perversity while recording evidence as appellant/ injured could not prove permanent disability to extent of 20%, however,

regarding being had to the nature of the accident, injuries suffered and material on record, in the interest of justice, a lump-sump amount of Rs. 50,000/- (Rs. Fifty Thousand Only) is awarded in addition to the amount already awarded by the tribunal i.e. Rs. 76,974/- alongwith the interest at the rate of 7% per annum as fixed by the Tribunal from the date of filing of application till its realization.

The enhanced amount of compensation i.e. Rs.50,000/- (Rs. Fifty Thousand Only) shall be payable to appellant/ claimant within a period of three months from the date of production of certified copy of the order passed today.
Rest of the award passed by the Tribunal shall remain intact.
6. With the aforesaid, the Miscellaneous appeal is partly allowed and disposed of.

(ROHIT ARYA) JUDGE Prachi PRACHI MISHRA 2023.01.23 18:03:04 +05'30'
